A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnoPLe despite the changed title, and their main text, equations, figures and tables are readable. V1 includes supplementary Sections 6–10. V2 ends with references while referring to supplementary implementation details, visual comparisons and discussion that are not supplied, limiting comparison of those materials.

before.justification: V1 reports original AnoPLe experiments on MVTec-AD and VisA, including benchmark results, component ablations, sensitivity studies and qualitative failure analysis in the supplement.

after.justification: V2 reports original AnoPLe benchmark results, ablations, held-out-category evaluations, medical-domain experiments and inference-speed measurements. Its use of previously reported results for some baselines does not negate these original outcomes.

M1.justification: The documented algorithm retains bidirectional textual–visual prompt coupling, pixel- and latent-space pseudo anomalies, the lightweight decoder, three loss terms and memory-assisted scoring. V2's scale-aware prefix corresponds to v1's multi-view signal, including the same training crops and global-only inference. Renaming and rewritten explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: V2 adds Real-IAD and medical anomaly detection on BMAD's Brain MRI, Liver CT and Retinal OCT datasets to the retained MVTec-AD and VisA coverage. These additions substantially broaden the represented domains and imaging modalities. Multi-class anomaly detection itself was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: The main Table 1 comparison removes PaDiM, RegAD, FastRecon, AnomalyGPT and InCTRL and adds IIPAD and INP-Former, retaining SPADE, PatchCore, WinCLIP and PromptAD. V2's medical comparison also evaluates MedCLIP and UniVAD. These are substantial changes in evaluated comparator membership, independently of changed scores.

E3.justification: V2 Table 1 reports reproduced MVTec-AD/VisA baselines under a unified multi-class training configuration, replacing v1's comparison mixing single-class, multi-class and transfer settings. V2 adds image AUPR and pixel PRO, plus leave-one-class-out and targeted anomaly-description-withholding protocols. The retained backbone and image/crop resolutions do not establish changed AnoPLe training settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds held-out-category generalization tests, targeted defect-description withholding tests and analysis of PromptAD's multi-class embedding confusion. The class-name-versus-object ablation and prefix-attention analysis already existed in v1's supplement and are not new analyses. Whether v1's additional sensitivity, pseudo-anomaly and failure studies persist cannot be checked without v2's referenced supplement.

E5.justification: V1 Table 1 and supplementary Tables 6–9 report ± uncertainty terms, whereas v2 Table 1 contains point estimates only. The unavailable v2 supplement prevents determining whether uncertainty reporting was removed overall or relocated. Neither supplied text establishes a change in repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Reported one-shot AnoPLe image/pixel AUROC changes from 94.1/95.3 to 94.5/96.0 on MVTec-AD and from 86.2/95.8 to 86.0/97.0 on VisA. V2 also adds Real-IAD, medical, held-out-category and FPS results and revises ablation scores. These are substantial result changes; revised comparison protocols and incomplete training details preclude interpreting all differences as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The prompt projections, prefix definition, losses, local–global alignment and anomaly-score equations retain their mathematical substance. V2 reorganizes and renotates these expressions but introduces no new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes normal-only few-shot detection with performance close to existing state of the art. V2 makes scalable few-shot multi-class detection central and adds broad claims about unseen-category/anomaly robustness and medical applicability. These materially expand the claimed contribution, although multi-class operation and the principal method components already existed.

C2.justification: V2 develops explanations linking class semantics to reduced inter-class confusion and attributes INP-Former's generalization weaknesses to absent textual grounding. It also interprets medical results as evidence of transferable normality cues. These extend v1's mechanism discussion substantially. V1's explicit logical-anomaly, multiple-object and shape limitations have no accessible counterpart in v2; their status in the missing supplement is unknown.

D1.justification: V1 specifies epochs, learning rates, prompt settings, SGD parameters, memory layers, hardware and code access. V2 retains backbone and crop-size information but directs additional settings to an unavailable supplement; its readable text also lacks v1's code-access statement. The full extent of revised, removed or relocated reproducibility information cannot be determined.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work around multi-class anomaly detection, discussing CCL, IIPAD, INP-Former and UniVAD and adding medical-domain references. V1's emphasis on the prompt-learning lineage through MaPLe, VPT, CoOp and CoCoOp is reduced, with those references absent from v2's bibliography. This changes the research context beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten around multi-class scalability. Method subsections are reorganized, textual and visual prompting receive separate treatments, and multi-view signal becomes scale-aware prefix. New generalization and medical sections materially restructure the narrative.

P2.justification: V2 replaces Figure 1 with semantic, speed and embedding panels, redraws the architecture figure, and restructures Table 1 around shot settings and additional metrics. Qualitative figures and ablation tables are redesigned. V2 Figure 5 redisplays the MVTec portion of v1 supplementary Figure 12, rather than introducing a new attention visualization.

improvement.justification: V2 adds valuable unified comparisons, generalization tests and medical evaluations, but uncertainty and reproducibility information are less accessible. Its stronger interpretation also exceeds some reported evidence: Section 4.2 describes INP-Former advantages as 0.1–1.0 points, while Table 1 gives 88.3 versus 83.2 image AUROC on 4-shot Real-IAD. These reliability concerns and the unavailable supplement prevent a confident net quality judgment despite the broader empirical coverage.
